cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The new rule will ____ every student. (affect / effect)
cards.back: affect
cards.note: Verb meaning 'to influence'. 'Effect' is usually a noun meaning result: 'the effect of the rule'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Everyone ____ Riya has submitted the form. (accept / except)
cards.back: except
cards.note: 'Except' means 'other than'. 'Accept' means to receive or agree to.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The ____ addressed the school assembly. (principal / principle)
cards.back: principal
cards.note: 'Principal' is the head of a school; also 'main'. 'Principle' is a rule or belief.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The bus remained ____ at the signal. (stationary / stationery)
cards.back: stationary
cards.note: 'Stationary' means not moving. 'Stationery' means pens, paper and writing materials.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The soup and the bread ____ each other well. (complement / compliment)
cards.back: complement
cards.note: 'Complement' means to complete or go well with. 'Compliment' means praise.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Please ____ me what to do next. (advice / advise)
cards.back: advise
cards.note: 'Advise' is the verb. 'Advice' is the noun: 'good advice'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Be ____ about the matter; it is confidential. (discreet / discrete)
cards.back: discreet
cards.note: 'Discreet' means careful and tactful. 'Discrete' means separate and distinct.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: She sought legal ____ before signing. (council / counsel)
cards.back: counsel
cards.note: 'Counsel' means advice (or a lawyer). 'Council' is an elected or advisory body.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Do not ____ your keys again. (lose / loose)
cards.back: lose
cards.note: 'Lose' (verb) means to fail to keep. 'Loose' (adjective) means not tight.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Do you need any ____ information? (farther / further)
cards.back: further
cards.note: 'Further' means additional. 'Farther' is used for physical distance: 'walk farther'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The dog wagged ____ tail. (its / it's)
cards.back: its
cards.note: 'Its' is possessive. 'It's' is the short form of 'it is' or 'it has'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: She is taller ____ her brother. (then / than)
cards.back: than
cards.note: 'Than' is used in comparisons. 'Then' refers to time: 'first this, then that'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: ____ bag is this? (whose / who's)
cards.back: Whose
cards.note: 'Whose' shows possession. 'Who's' is the short form of 'who is' or 'who has'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: He was ____ the captain of the school team. (formally / formerly)
cards.back: formerly
cards.note: 'Formerly' means earlier or in the past. 'Formally' means in an official or proper way.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The teacher tried to ____ a response from the class. (elicit / illicit)
cards.back: elicit
cards.note: 'Elicit' means to draw out. 'Illicit' means illegal or forbidden.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The company is hiring more ____. (personal / personnel)
cards.back: personnel
cards.note: 'Personnel' means staff or employees. 'Personal' means private or individual.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Please ____ to the exit in an orderly manner. (precede / proceed)
cards.back: proceed
cards.note: 'Proceed' means to go ahead. 'Precede' means to come before.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: A storm is ____; stay indoors. (eminent / imminent)
cards.back: imminent
cards.note: 'Imminent' means about to happen. 'Eminent' means distinguished or well known.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The engineer found an ____ solution to the problem. (ingenious / ingenuous)
cards.back: ingenious
cards.note: 'Ingenious' means clever and inventive. 'Ingenuous' means innocent and frank.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The machine ran in a ____ stream all night without a break. (continual / continuous)
cards.back: continuous
cards.note: 'Continuous' means without a break. 'Continual' means happening repeatedly, with pauses.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: She has ____ the loss with great courage. (born / borne)
cards.back: borne
cards.note: 'Borne' (from 'bear') means carried or endured. 'Born' means brought into life.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: They tried to ____ a plan to save water. (device / devise)
cards.back: devise
cards.note: 'Devise' (verb) means to plan or invent. 'Device' (noun) is a gadget or tool.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Take a deep ____ before you begin. (breath / breathe)
cards.back: breath
cards.note: 'Breath' (noun) is the air taken in. 'Breathe' (verb) is the act of taking in air.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: I wonder ____ it will rain today. (weather / whether)
cards.back: whether
cards.note: 'Whether' introduces alternatives. 'Weather' means the state of the atmosphere.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: We had ice cream for ____. (dessert / desert)
cards.back: dessert
cards.note: 'Dessert' is a sweet course at the end of a meal. 'Desert' is dry land, or to abandon.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Please ____ the book on the table. (lay / lie)
cards.back: lay
cards.note: 'Lay' means to put something down and takes an object. 'Lie' means to recline.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: ____ Hindi, she speaks French and Tamil. (Beside / Besides)
cards.back: Besides
cards.note: 'Besides' means in addition to. 'Beside' means next to.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: There are ____ students in class today than yesterday. (fewer / less)
cards.back: fewer
cards.note: Use 'fewer' with countable nouns (students) and 'less' with uncountable nouns (water).

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Please ____ that the door is locked before you leave. (assure / ensure)
cards.back: ensure
cards.note: 'Ensure' means to make certain. 'Assure' means to promise someone. 'Insure' is to cover with insurance.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The ____ for the new school has been chosen. (site / sight)
cards.back: site
cards.note: 'Site' is a location. 'Sight' is vision; 'cite' means to quote.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The sun will ____ at six tomorrow. (raise / rise)
cards.back: rise
cards.note: 'Rise' does not take an object. 'Raise' needs an object: 'raise the flag'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Of the two options, I prefer the ____. (later / latter)
cards.back: latter
cards.note: 'Latter' means the second of two things named. 'Later' means after some time.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: It is ____ cold this morning. (quiet / quite)
cards.back: quite
cards.note: 'Quite' means fairly or completely. 'Quiet' means silent.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'each', 'every', 'either' and 'neither' take which kind of verb?
cards.back:
A singular verb.
Wrong: Each of the players have a medal.
Right: Each of the players has a medal.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: a collective noun (committee, team, class) acting as a unit takes which verb?
cards.back:
A singular verb, with 'its'.
Wrong: The committee have made their decision.
Right: The committee has made its decision.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: after 'one of the' + plural noun, which verb is used?
cards.back:
A singular verb, because the subject is 'one'.
Wrong: One of my friends are a doctor.
Right: One of my friends is a doctor.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb. What is the exception?
cards.back:
When the two words together name one thing or idea, the verb is singular.
Wrong: Bread and butter are my usual breakfast.
Right: Bread and butter is my usual breakfast.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: with 'neither...nor' and 'either...or', the verb agrees with which subject?
cards.back:
The subject nearer to the verb.
Wrong: Neither the teacher nor the students was present.
Right: Neither the teacher nor the students were present.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: with 'as well as', 'along with' and 'together with', the verb agrees with which subject?
cards.back:
The first subject, not the phrase that follows.
Wrong: The teacher, along with her students, are going on the trip.
Right: The teacher, along with her students, is going on the trip.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'advice', 'information', 'furniture' and 'news' are uncountable. Can they take a plural form?
cards.back:
No. They have no plural and take a singular verb.
Wrong: She gave me many advices about the exam.
Right: She gave me a lot of advice about the exam.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: when is 'for' used and when is 'since' used?
cards.back:
'Since' marks a point in time; 'for' marks a period of time.
Wrong: I have lived here since ten years.
Right: I have lived here for ten years.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which tense goes with 'since' for an action that began in the past and continues?
cards.back:
The present perfect (or present perfect continuous), not the simple present.
Wrong: He is ill since Monday.
Right: He has been ill since Monday.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which form of 'be' follows 'wish' for an unreal present wish?
cards.back:
'Were' for all persons.
Wrong: I wish I was taller.
Right: I wish I were taller.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: what is the pattern of an unreal present condition (type 2)?
cards.back:
If + past tense, would + base verb; use 'were' for 'be'.
Wrong: If I was you, I will apologise.
Right: If I were you, I would apologise.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'a' or 'an' depends on what?
cards.back:
The sound, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.
Wrong: He waited for a hour at an university.
Right: He waited for an hour at a university.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which preposition follows 'different'?
cards.back:
'From', not 'than'.
Wrong: Her view is different than mine.
Right: Her view is different from mine.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: meaning 'talk over', 'be present at', 'go into', 'arrive at', do discuss, attend, enter, reach take a preposition?
cards.back:
No. In these senses they are followed directly by the object.
Wrong: We discussed about the problem.
Right: We discussed the problem.
cards.note: Other senses differ: 'attend to' (deal with) and 'enter into' (begin, e.g. an agreement) take a preposition.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'superior', 'inferior', 'senior', 'junior' and 'prefer' take which word before the second item?
cards.back:
'To', not 'than'.
Wrong: This phone is superior than that one.
Right: This phone is superior to that one.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: can a comparative or superlative be formed twice (more + -er)?
cards.back:
No. Use one form only.
Wrong: This book is more better than that one.
Right: This book is better than that one.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which pronoun case follows a preposition?
cards.back:
The objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
Wrong: The secret is between you and I.
Right: The secret is between you and me.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: items in a list must have what kind of form?
cards.back:
The same grammatical form (parallel structure).
Wrong: She likes reading, writing and to swim.
Right: She likes reading, writing and swimming.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'No sooner' is followed by which structure and which conjunction?
cards.back:
Past perfect (inverted) + 'than'.
Wrong: No sooner had he left when it began to rain.
Right: No sooner had he left than it began to rain.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'Hardly' and 'scarcely' are followed by which conjunction?
cards.back:
'When' (or 'before'), not 'than'.
Wrong: Hardly had she entered than the bell rang.
Right: Hardly had she entered when the bell rang.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'many a' is followed by which noun and verb forms?
cards.back:
A singular noun and a singular verb.
Wrong: Many a student have failed this test.
Right: Many a student has failed this test.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: distances, sums of money and periods of time treated as a whole take which verb?
cards.back:
A singular verb.
Wrong: Ten kilometres are a long distance to walk.
Right: Ten kilometres is a long distance to walk.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: names of subjects like Mathematics and Physics, and 'news', take which verb?
cards.back:
A singular verb, despite the -s ending.
Wrong: Mathematics are my favourite subject.
Right: Mathematics is my favourite subject.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: how do 'the number of' and 'a number of' differ in verb agreement?
cards.back:
'The number of' takes a singular verb; 'a number of' takes a plural verb.
Wrong: The number of students are rising every year.
Right: The number of students is rising every year.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: a participle phrase at the start must describe which noun?
cards.back:
The subject of the main clause that follows it.
Wrong: Having finished the work, the lights were switched off.
Right: Having finished the work, he switched off the lights.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows a preposition?
cards.back:
The gerund (-ing form), not the infinitive.
Wrong: She is fond of to sing.
Right: She is fond of singing.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which pronoun case follows 'let'?
cards.back:
The objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
Wrong: Let he and I go.
Right: Let him and me go.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which tense follows 'It is high time'?
cards.back:
The simple past.
Wrong: It is high time we leave.
Right: It is high time we left.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which part of speech modifies a verb?
cards.back:
An adverb (usually -ly), not an adjective.
Wrong: She sings beautiful.
Right: She sings beautifully.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows 'would rather'?
cards.back:
The base form without 'to'.
Wrong: I would rather to stay home.
Right: I would rather stay home.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'lucid' mean?
cards.back: (of language) transparently clear; easily understandable

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'concise' mean?
cards.back: Expressing much in few words

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'coherent' mean?
cards.back: Marked by an orderly, logical, and aesthetically consistent relation of parts

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'ambiguous' mean?
cards.back: Having more than one possible meaning

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'obscure' mean?
cards.back: Not clearly understood or expressed

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'candid' mean?
cards.back: Characterized by directness in manner or speech; without subtlety or evasion

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'sceptical' mean?
cards.back: Marked by or given to doubt

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'gullible' mean?
cards.back: Easily tricked because of being too trusting

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'reluctant' mean?
cards.back: Not eager

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'benevolent' mean?
cards.back: Intending or showing kindness

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'impartial' mean?
cards.back: Showing lack of favoritism

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'biased' mean?
cards.back: Favoring one person or side over another

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'arbitrary' mean?

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'rational' mean?
cards.back: Consistent with or based on or using reason

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'prudent' mean?
cards.back: Careful and sensible; marked by sound judgment

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'diligent' mean?
cards.back: Characterized by care and perseverance in carrying out tasks

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'meticulous' mean?
cards.back: Marked by extreme care in treatment of details

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'tenacious' mean?
cards.back: Stubbornly unyielding

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'lethargic' mean?
cards.back: Deficient in alertness or activity

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'resilient' mean?
cards.back: Recovering readily from adversity, depression, or the like

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'abundant' mean?
cards.back: Present in great quantity

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'scarce' mean?
cards.back: Deficient in quantity or number compared with the demand

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'substantial' mean?
cards.back: Fairly large

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'trivial' mean?
cards.back: Of little substance or significance

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'frugal' mean?
cards.back: Avoiding waste

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'transient' mean?
cards.back: Lasting a very short time

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'durable' mean?
cards.back: Existing for a long time

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'perpetual' mean?
cards.back: Uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'obsolete' mean?
cards.back: No longer in use

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'inevitable' mean?
cards.back: Incapable of being avoided or prevented

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'eloquent' mean?
cards.back: Fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'ephemeral' mean?
cards.back: Lasting for a very short time

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'ubiquitous' mean?
cards.back: Present or found everywhere

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'pragmatic' mean?
cards.back: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'verbose' mean?
cards.back: Using more words than are needed

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'aloof' mean?
cards.back: Distant and reserved; not friendly or involved

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'ardent' mean?
cards.back: Very enthusiastic or passionate

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'audacious' mean?
cards.back: Showing a bold willingness to take risks

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'austere' mean?
cards.back: Strict or severe in manner; plain, without luxury

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'avarice' mean?
cards.back: Extreme greed for wealth or gain

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'benign' mean?
cards.back: Gentle and harmless; not dangerous

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'blithe' mean?
cards.back: Cheerful and carefree

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'brevity' mean?
cards.back: Shortness of time or of expression

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'callous' mean?
cards.back: Showing cruel indifference to the feelings of others

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'cogent' mean?
cards.back: Clear, logical and convincing

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'complacent' mean?
cards.back: Smugly satisfied with oneself and unaware of dangers

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'conspicuous' mean?
cards.back: Easily seen; clearly visible

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'contemptuous' mean?
cards.back: Showing that one thinks someone or something is unworthy of respect

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'copious' mean?
cards.back: Abundant in supply or quantity

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'cynical' mean?
cards.back: Believing that people act only from self-interest

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'daunting' mean?
cards.back: Seeming difficult to deal with; intimidating

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'dearth' mean?
cards.back: A scarcity or lack of something

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'defer' mean?
cards.back: To put off to a later time

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'deplore' mean?
cards.back: To feel or express strong disapproval of

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'detrimental' mean?
cards.back: Causing harm or damage

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'discreet' mean?
cards.back: Careful and prudent in what one says or does; able to keep secrets

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'diverse' mean?
cards.back: Showing a great deal of variety

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'dormant' mean?
cards.back: Temporarily inactive; in a state of rest

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'eccentric' mean?
cards.back: Unconventional and slightly strange

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'elusive' mean?
cards.back: Difficult to find, catch or achieve

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'eminent' mean?
cards.back: Famous and respected within a particular field

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'empathy' mean?
cards.back: The ability to understand and share another person's feelings

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'endeavour' mean?
cards.back: A serious attempt or effort to achieve something

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'enigma' mean?
cards.back: A person or thing that is mysterious and difficult to understand

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'equivocal' mean?
cards.back: Open to more than one interpretation; deliberately vague

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'exemplary' mean?
cards.back: Serving as a desirable model; very good

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'exhaustive' mean?
cards.back: Thorough and covering every detail

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'exuberant' mean?
cards.back: Full of energy, excitement and cheerfulness

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'fastidious' mean?
cards.back: Very attentive to accuracy and detail; hard to please

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'feasible' mean?
cards.back: Possible and practical to do

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'fickle' mean?
cards.back: Changing often, especially in loyalty or affection

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'frivolous' mean?
cards.back: Not having any serious purpose or value

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'futile' mean?
cards.back: Incapable of producing any useful result

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'garrulous' mean?
cards.back: Excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'gregarious' mean?
cards.back: Fond of company; sociable

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'hostile' mean?
cards.back: Unfriendly; showing opposition

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'humble' mean?
cards.back: Having a modest view of one's own importance

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'hypocrisy' mean?
cards.back: Pretending to have virtues or beliefs that one does not really have

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'impeccable' mean?
cards.back: In accordance with the highest standards; faultless

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'impetuous' mean?
cards.back: Acting quickly and without thought or care

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'indigenous' mean?
cards.back: Originating or occurring naturally in a particular place

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'indolent' mean?
cards.back: Wanting to avoid activity or exertion; lazy

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'inept' mean?
cards.back: Having or showing no skill; clumsy

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'intrepid' mean?
cards.back: Fearless and adventurous

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'jubilant' mean?
cards.back: Feeling or expressing great happiness and triumph

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'lenient' mean?
cards.back: More merciful or tolerant than expected

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'lucrative' mean?
cards.back: Producing a great deal of profit

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'magnanimous' mean?
cards.back: Generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or someone less powerful

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'meagre' mean?
cards.back: Lacking in quantity or quality

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'melancholy' mean?
cards.back: A feeling of pensive sadness, typically with no obvious cause

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'mundane' mean?
cards.back: Lacking interest or excitement; dull and ordinary

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'nonchalant' mean?
cards.back: Calm and unconcerned; not showing interest or anxiety

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'notorious' mean?
cards.back: Famous or well known for something bad

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'novice' mean?
cards.back: A person new to or inexperienced in a field or situation

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'oblivious' mean?
cards.back: Not aware of or concerned about what is happening around one

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'obstinate' mean?
cards.back: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'ominous' mean?
cards.back: Giving the impression that something bad is going to happen

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'opulent' mean?
cards.back: Ostentatiously rich and luxurious

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'ostentatious' mean?
cards.back: Designed to impress or attract notice; showy

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'pacify' mean?
cards.back: To calm down or quiet someone who is angry or upset

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'pensive' mean?
cards.back: Engaged in deep or serious thought

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'pertinent' mean?

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a blessing in disguise' mean?

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a bolt from the blue' mean?
cards.back: A sudden and completely unexpected event, usually an unwelcome one
cards.note: Example: The news of the closure came like a bolt from the blue.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a piece of cake' mean?
cards.back: Something very easy to do
cards.note: Example: The maths paper was a piece of cake for her.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'Achilles' heel' mean?
cards.back: A person's weak point or vulnerable spot
cards.note: Example: Overconfidence is his Achilles' heel.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'at the eleventh hour' mean?
cards.back: At the last possible moment
cards.note: Example: They submitted the form at the eleventh hour.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'beat about the bush' mean?
cards.back: To avoid coming to the main point
cards.note: Example: Stop beating about the bush and tell me what happened.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'bite the bullet' mean?
cards.back: To face something unpleasant bravely
cards.note: Example: She decided to bite the bullet and take the exam again.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'break the ice' mean?
cards.back: To start a conversation in an awkward or formal situation
cards.note: Example: A joke from the host broke the ice at the meeting.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'burn the midnight oil' mean?
cards.back: To study or work late into the night
cards.note: Example: He burnt the midnight oil before the board exams.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'by leaps and bounds' mean?
cards.back: Very quickly and in large steps
cards.note: Example: Her English has improved by leaps and bounds.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'call it a day' mean?
cards.back: To stop working for the day
cards.note: Example: We have done enough; let us call it a day.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'cry over spilt milk' mean?
cards.back: To regret something that cannot be undone
cards.note: Example: There is no use crying over spilt milk now.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'cut a sorry figure' mean?
cards.back: To make a poor impression; to appear in an unfavourable way
cards.note: Example: He cut a sorry figure after failing in front of everyone.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a dark horse' mean?
cards.back: A person with unexpected qualities or abilities, especially a little-known winner
cards.note: Example: Nobody expected Rahul to win; he was a dark horse.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'draw the line' mean?
cards.back: To set a limit on what one will accept
cards.note: Example: I can help you, but I draw the line at cheating.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'eat humble pie' mean?
cards.back: To apologise humbly and admit one's mistake
cards.note: Example: He had to eat humble pie and apologise to the teacher.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'face the music' mean?
cards.back: To accept the consequences or punishment for one's actions
cards.note: Example: He broke the window and had to face the music.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'fish in troubled waters' mean?
cards.back: To take advantage of a confused or difficult situation for personal gain
cards.note: Example: Some leaders fish in troubled waters during a crisis.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'get cold feet' mean?
cards.back: To lose courage at the last moment
cards.note: Example: He got cold feet just before the interview.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'hit the nail on the head' mean?
cards.back: To say or do exactly the right thing
cards.note: Example: You hit the nail on the head when you called it a lack of planning.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'in hot water' mean?
cards.back: In trouble
cards.note: Example: He is in hot water for missing the deadline.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'kill two birds with one stone' mean?
cards.back: To achieve two aims with a single action
cards.note: Example: By cycling to college, she kills two birds with one stone: exercise and travel.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'leave no stone unturned' mean?
cards.back: To try every possible means to achieve something
cards.note: Example: The police left no stone unturned in the search.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'let the cat out of the bag' mean?
cards.back: To reveal a secret by mistake
cards.note: Example: He let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'make a clean breast of' mean?

cards.note: Example: The thief made a clean breast of his crime.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'once in a blue moon' mean?

cards.note: Example: We meet once in a blue moon.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'out of the blue' mean?

cards.note: Example: An old friend called me out of the blue.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'pull someone's leg' mean?

cards.note: Example: Are you serious or are you pulling my leg?

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'rain cats and dogs' mean?
cards.back: To rain very heavily
cards.note: Example: It was raining cats and dogs, so we stayed indoors.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'rub salt into the wound' mean?
cards.back: To make a painful situation worse
cards.note: Example: Criticising him after his defeat only rubbed salt into the wound.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'see eye to eye' mean?
cards.back: To agree with someone
cards.note: Example: The two partners rarely see eye to eye.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'spill the beans' mean?
cards.back: To reveal a secret
cards.note: Example: Someone spilled the beans about the results.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'take with a pinch of salt' mean?
cards.back: To not believe something completely
cards.note: Example: Take his claims with a pinch of salt.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'the last straw' mean?
cards.back: The final problem that makes a situation unbearable
cards.note: Example: His rude reply was the last straw.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'throw in the towel' mean?
cards.back: To give up; to admit defeat
cards.note: Example: After three attempts he threw in the towel.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'turn a deaf ear' mean?
cards.back: To refuse to listen or pay attention
cards.note: Example: The officer turned a deaf ear to their complaints.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'under the weather' mean?
cards.back: Slightly unwell
cards.note: Example: She stayed home because she was feeling under the weather.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a white elephant' mean?
cards.back: A costly possession that is useless and difficult to maintain
cards.note: Example: The unused stadium became a white elephant.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a wild goose chase' mean?
cards.back: A useless search for something that cannot be found
cards.note: Example: The clue led us on a wild goose chase.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'add fuel to the fire' mean?
cards.back: To make a bad situation worse
cards.note: Example: His angry comment added fuel to the fire.

cards.subject: english

cards.subject: english

cards.subject: english

cards.subject: english

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'hold one's horses' mean?
cards.back: To wait; to be patient
cards.note: Example: Hold your horses, we have not started yet.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'jump the gun' mean?

cards.note: Example: Do not jump the gun; wait for the official result.

cards.subject: english

cards.note: Example: We have broken the back of the project.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'to bell the cat' mean?
cards.back: To take the risk of doing a dangerous task for the benefit of the group
cards.note: Example: Nobody dared to bell the cat and confront the manager.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a cock and bull story' mean?
cards.back: An absurd, unbelievable story made up as an excuse
cards.note: Example: He gave us a cock and bull story about the lost homework.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a storm in a teacup' mean?
cards.back: Great excitement or anger over a trivial matter
cards.note: Example: The whole dispute was a storm in a teacup.

cards.subject: english

cards.back: Feelings of hatred or hostility between people
cards.note: Example: There is bad blood between the two families.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a feather in one's cap' mean?
cards.back: An achievement to be proud of
